note: A ratio, not a count. Absolute survivor counts rise with every
line added -- new code means new mutants, so a healthy change
with good tests would trip an absolute ratchet. The score below
is killed / (killed + survived): it stays comparable as the
codebase grows and only moves when tests get better or worse.
Not every survivor is a gap. About a quarter only change a log
or error message, which nothing asserts on by design. Others are
equivalent: `if not mismatched` decides when the read-back loop
exits, not what it returns, so killing it would mean asserting on
timing -- a worse test than the mutant is a risk.
Mutants with no covering test are excluded from the score rather
than counted as failures: the tests that drive a module through a
real subprocess load the original source, so a mutation run says
nothing about what they cover. See
docs/decisions/0005-mutation-testing-scope.md.
0.64 -> 0.65 (2026-08-17). THE SCORE ROSE WHILE THE CODEBASE GREW,
which is the opposite of what the previous re-baseline found and
worth writing down for the same reason.
Three modules landed between the runs -- registers, reconcile and
backend, 660 new mutants. New code normally drags a ratio down: it
arrives with fewer tests than the code that has been shot at for
two releases. These did not. not_covered stayed at 82, so none of
them is structurally out of reach, and the score went 0.643 ->
0.655 with 176 more mutants killed than the growth alone explains.
The likely reason is what those modules are: pure functions checked
against recorded device dumps, rather than code that opens sockets
and reads clocks. A test that can assert an exact value kills
mutants; a test that can only assert 'it did not hang' does not.
That is an argument for pushing more logic into that shape, and the
number is the evidence for it.

why_it_moved: That run was itself a re-baseline, from 0.728 over a third of the
runtime to 0.643 over all of it: not_covered fell 677 -> 81 as
four modules came under evaluation for the first time. 0.728 was
never a measurement of this runtime.

note: Measured independently on a GitHub runner. Five mutants differ,
which is the timing-sensitive tail: the suite binds real UDP
sockets and drives threads. not_covered agrees exactly, and that
is the number a re-baseline turns on.

floor_note: The gate is min_score - tolerance = 0.64. That is the number that
matters: the score may not fall below it. min_score itself is set
at the measured 0.655 rounded down, so the policy neither fails
nor nags on the run it was recorded from -- a baseline that prints
'raise me' on every CI run teaches people to ignore it.
